input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — the playbook walk-away position. It also conflicts with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and with § 9.4's unconditional convenience-termination right and § 7.1's bar on minimum-use charges. We propose the preferred position: no minimum commitment, with Fees owed only for Services ordered and actually used, leaving the fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up) available in negotiation.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year USD 2M take-or-pay minimum commitment; fees payable only for Services ordered and used.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have replaced the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment with a confirmation that Fees are owed only for Services actually ordered and used, since we do not accept minimum purchase commitments without an exit and § 12.3 already records that we have made no minimum-volume commitment. If Copperleaf needs a commitment, we can consider one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice under § 9.4, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

ops.oldText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: 2.1 Customer makes no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment. Customer owes Fees only for Services it orders under an Order Form and for actual usage, and may reduce or terminate any Order Form in accordance with Section 9.4.
